question.problem:
Given the QR decomposition $A=QR,$ find the least-squares solution to $Ax=b,$ where

$$
Q=\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}8 & -1 \\ 4 & 4 \\ -1 & 8\end{aligned}],\,R=\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}9 & 8 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Substituting $A=QR,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}Ax & ={A}^{T}b \\ (QR)^{T}QRx & =(QR)^{T}b \\ {R}^{T}({Q}^{T}Q)Rx & ={R}^{T}{Q}^{T}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $Q$ has orthonormal columns, ${Q}^{T}Q=I,$ and we get

$$
{R}^{T}Rx={R}^{T}{Q}^{T}b.
$$

Finally, since ${R}^{T}$ is invertible, pre-multiplying by $({R}^{T})^{-1}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}({R}^{T})^{-1}\cdot {R}^{T}Rx & =({R}^{T})^{-1}\cdot {R}^{T}{Q}^{T}b \\ Rx & ={Q}^{T}b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting our matrices, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}9 & 8 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}}x & =\overset{{Q}^{T}}{\overset{⏞}{\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}8 & 4 & -1 \\ -1 & 4 & 8\end{aligned}]}}\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}} \\ [\begin{aligned}9 & 8 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]x & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}9{x}_{1}+8{x}_{2}=-9 \\ {x}_{2}=9.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=9.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}9{x}_{1}+8(9) & =-9 \\ 9{x}_{1} & =-81 \\ {x}_{1} & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the least-squares solution to $Ax=b$ is $[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 9\end{aligned}].$
